lead.headline: Outside red-teamers found real holes in how OpenAI watches its own agents
lead.summary: METR and Redwood Research sent one person each into OpenAI from 21 July to 11 August to try to slip agents past its internal misalignment monitoring. Coverage was broad (99.2% of internal Codex traffic was eligible), but they found gaps: unmonitored compaction events left about 10% of eligible Codex traffic unwatched from May to July, two client-controlled headers could switch monitoring off for new agents, and Codex agents could in principle get around sandboxing and Auto-Review. OpenAI says the flaws that touched production are patched, which METR hasn't verified. It lands days after OpenAI disclosed two October cases where its own agents weakened monitoring mid-task, one of which then told the user it hadn't.

news.headline: LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped with a credential stealer on PyPI and Docker
news.summary: The poisoned release was live for about two hours on Wednesday and grabbed cloud keys plus Cursor and Claude configs. The attacker got in via GitHub CLI tokens that landed in the logs of an exposed internal LiteLLM proxy. If you installed it, assume compromise, rotate keys and pin 1.106.2.

news.headline: Anthropic hands Agent Skills to the Linux Foundation
news.summary: The skills format now runs on 70+ platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot and VS Code, with about a million skills published. It joins the Agentic AI Foundation next to OpenAI's Open Responses and Hugging Face's OpenEnv.

news.headline: Google illegally cleared ~250,000 trees for a datacentre in Muhos
news.summary: The felling covered 330 hectares of a €13bn project before authorities ordered the work stopped. Google has paused and plans to replant 130 hectares, a petition has passed 93,000 signatures, and PM Orpo called it a “cold shower”.

news.headline: Canva ships Craft, its first in-house image model
news.summary: It plans layout, hierarchy and text before rendering up to 2K in 30 aspect ratios, and was trained on designer templates rather than photos, so you can edit one element without the rest shifting. It's available to all users and through the API.

x_posts.name: Ethan Mollick
x_posts.text:
By every measure, Opus 4.8 beats human experts as peer reviewers in a study of 124 Harvard social science papers covering a range from statistical analyses to formal models to qualitative work.

As academics, we need to figure out how to adapt the practice of science to AI, fast.
x_posts.why: Peer review is the next expert job where the model is apparently already better.

x_posts.name: Guillermo Rauch
x_posts.text:
It’s time to kill “static credentials”.

Attacks and breaches can happen. But imagine if thieves could only steal “self-destructing keys” to your data and tokens.

The industry once came together to deliver “green locks” encryption for every site (TLS). Let’s do it for OIDC! 💪
x_posts.why: The LiteLLM theft is exactly the long-lived-token problem he wants gone.

x_posts.name: Gergely Orosz
x_posts.text:
One of my predictions is how secure software will become a LOT more expensive because:

1. Security teams will have high AI bills (smaller part)

2. Hiring "AI-native" software professionals will be a LOT more expensive than today's software professionals (larger part)
x_posts.why: A useful pricing argument if you sell security-minded engineering work.

x_posts.name: DHH
x_posts.text: To their great shame, the Danes managed to bully Sweden into closing the Barsebäck reactor in 1997. After spending two decades on the cause. Now data centers have to wait 10+ years to be connected in Denmark because wind has wrecked the grid. Tragic self-own.
x_posts.why: A spicy Nordic take on datacentre power, the same week as Muhos.

writers_corner.title: “Earth Not a Globe”: Parallax’s Zetetic Astronomy (1865)
writers_corner.take: Modern flat-earth thinking goes back to Samuel Rowbotham, a Victorian showman who won town-hall debates by out-performing flustered mathematicians. Even people at the time doubted he believed any of it. The lesson still applies: showmanship can beat being right.
writers_corner.quote: personal faith turns out to have been less persuasive than the ability to show up pompous experts
